brief: Goldman's Global Reflections argues compounders will keep beating high-growth cyclicals as growth scarcity persists. Its AI-over-cyclicals call (SPXXAI) has worked and stays live. Soft PCE/NFP data pushed out the Fed's next hike, but rate-sensitive equities (Homebuilders -17.5% in 3 months, Non-Profitable Tech -11.4% since July) sold off in the broader rates selloff. GS likes a sector-neutral beta basket (GSPUBETA), hedged via Beta-ex AI (GSPUBETX), for relief if yields ease further. AI power fundamentals stay intact. GS sees 108GW of 2030 datacenter demand (23% CAGR) and GEV guiding to 125GW of backlog (6x capacity), as IPP and gas-infra valuations derated 30% and 13%. GS likes the theme into FERC/PJM, 3Q earnings, midterm and ERCOT catalysts and launched an Asia battery-backup basket. OAT-Bund spreads near 150bps show contagion into BTPs, pressuring crowded European bank longs. GS would buy EU bank dips if French fiscal risk stays contained, but stays cautious on weak-balance-sheet names. Japan's AI leadership and gradual BoJ normalization separate it from the rest of Asia, led by its Optical Networking basket. China's Golden Week data is the next catalyst. A widening production-consumption gap reflects a manufacturing pivot that hurts consumption, supporting shorts on Asia Consumer Inertia.
